sections.h2: What kind of housing market does Daviess County have?
sections.html:
Daviess County is western Kentucky's river-city market. Owensboro is the seat and the largest city, and the county forms the Owensboro metropolitan area on the Ohio River. It was carved out of Ohio County on January 14, 1815, and its name carries a spelling slip: the namesake, Joseph Hamilton Daveiss, was recorded with the wrong spelling at the state clerk's office and nobody corrected it.

The county covers 477 square miles, of which 18 are water. The northern half along the river is mostly flat, while the south turns to rolling hills and valleys where coal was once mined along Panther Creek. The Census Bureau counted 103,312 people in 2020 and estimated 104,898 for July 2025, up 1.5 percent.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Daviess County homes?
sections.html:
Census QuickFacts for 2020 to 2024 and 2025 list:

  • 45,155 housing units and 41,639 households
  • 68.1 percent owner-occupied, so nearly a third of households rent
  • Median value of an owner-occupied home: $199,900
  • Median gross rent: $918 a month
  • Median owner costs of $1,387 with a mortgage and $512 without
  • 253 building permits issued in 2025

At the median value, the Daviess County Fiscal Court's own real property rate of 12.2 cents per $100 works out to about $244 a year. School, city and special district rates come on top of that figure.

sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Daviess County?
sections.html:
The Daviess County Sheriff's Office tax division collects, from 212 St. Ann Street, Room 103, in Owensboro. The tax counter is open weekdays from 8:00 to 4:30 at 270-685-6133. The office is closed on Veterans Day, Thanksgiving, Black Friday, Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Year's Eve and New Year's Day.

Bills go out during the first week of November. Homeowners with an escrow account should ask the mortgage servicer before assuming a missing bill is lost, since the servicer may intend to pay it without requesting a copy. Property inside Owensboro also carries a city tax, which the City of Owensboro Tax Office handles at 270-687-8537.

sections.h2: What property tax rates did Daviess County set for 2025?
sections.html:
The Fiscal Court adopted the compensating rate for real property in August 2025, which lowered the county's rate from 12.9 cents to 12.2 cents per $100 of assessed value. Tangible personal property stayed at 13.8 cents per $100, and motor vehicles and watercraft at 17 cents per $100. The county described it as its largest tax cut in at least two decades.

Those rates are the county's share only. Your bill also includes taxing districts such as schools, so the total on a parcel is higher than 12.2 cents. Ask the sheriff's tax counter for a parcel-level bill, or look up the parcel on the sheriff's website, before you estimate a buyer's carrying cost.

sections.h2: What are the Daviess County payment dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Daviess County runs a calendar approved by the Kentucky Department of Revenue, and the dates repeat every year. Paying in the discount window saves 2 percent, while each missed window raises the cost.

Daviess County property tax collection periods (source: Daviess County Sheriff's Office, Tax Collection page)
PeriodWhat applies
November 10 to December 102 percent discount
December 11 to January 10Base amount
January 11 to February 105 percent penalty
February 11 to April 2521 percent penalty

A mailed payment counts as on time with a U.S. Postal Service postmark inside the period, under KRS 134.119. Returned checks carry a $25 fee and the bill reverts to unpaid.

sections.h2: How can I pay a Daviess County property tax bill?
sections.html:
You can pay online, in person, or by mail. The sheriff's website at dcsoky.gov has a Pay Taxes Online link, where several bills can share one cart and you can pay by card or electronic check. A fee is shown before you submit. The office warns that payments made on any other website will not be honored.

  • In person: cash, card, check, cashier's check or money order. Checks must match the exact amount.
  • By mail: make checks out to the Daviess County Sheriff's Office. The office takes checks only from U.S. banks.
  • Online: card or e-check on the sheriff's own site.

If you receive two bills for one parcel, an exemption may have been applied after the first printing, so read both and check the balance online.

sections.h2: How do I challenge a Daviess County assessment?
sections.html:
Start with the PVA office at 270-685-8474. Kentucky requires a conference with the PVA or a deputy before any appeal, and that conference has to fall in the May tax roll inspection period, which begins on the first Monday of May and lasts thirteen days. Real estate is valued as of January 1 at fair cash value.

After a conference that fails to settle the matter, you file at the County Clerk's office, 270-685-8434, by the end of the next workday after inspection closes. The local board of assessment appeals hears cases 25 to 35 days later. It decides on evidence, so bring comparable sales, an appraisal or repair estimates. If you disagree with the board, the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals is the next step.

sections.h2: Can a Daviess County homeowner reduce the taxable value?
sections.html:
Owners aged 65 or older, and owners classified as totally disabled, can claim the homestead exemption on the home they live in. For the 2025 and 2026 assessment years the exemption is $49,100. A house assessed at the county median of $199,900 would be taxed on $150,800.

File the application with the Daviess County PVA. Age is proved with a driver's license, birth certificate or passport. Disability claims need proof that a federal agency or a retirement system classified you as totally disabled.

sections.h2: What if I sell a Daviess County house after the bill is printed?
sections.html:
The sheriff's office advises anyone who sold or bought after January 1 and believes a bill arrived in error to ask the closing title company. Assessment happens on January 1 under KRS 132.220, so the paperwork can lag behind a sale. Your settlement statement should show the current year's tax split between seller and buyer.

Unpaid bills are mailed a delinquent notice on February 11. At the end of the business day on April 25 they move to the County Clerk, where substantial fees apply and the parcel can be sold at the county's tax sale. A delinquency can be paid off from the sale proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: What does a delinquent Daviess County bill turn into?
sections.html:
After April 25 the bill becomes a certificate of delinquency in the County Clerk's hands and a lien against the parcel. Under the state process, interest runs at 1 percent a month, with a 10 percent clerk fee and a 20 percent county attorney fee on top. The county attorney mails notices by mid-May and again by mid-June, and the owner may be able to set up installments.

From mid-July through late October the clerk can sell certificates to private buyers. The county must advertise the list in the local paper and on the clerk's website at least 30 days ahead of a sale. Once a certificate is sold, the owner pays the buyer, who adds substantial charges of its own. Anyone planning a sale of a house with a delinquency should aim to settle it before the summer sale dates.

faqs.q: When does the Daviess County 2 percent discount end?
faqs.a: It ends on December 10 each year. The period starts November 10, and bills are mailed in the first week of November.

faqs.q: What is the last day to pay a Daviess County property tax bill without turning it over to the clerk?
faqs.a: April 25, at the close of business. After that the unpaid bill goes to the County Clerk with added fees, and it becomes eligible for the tax sale.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Daviess County property taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes. Use the Pay Taxes Online link on the Daviess County Sheriff's Office site, dcsoky.gov. Card and e-check payments carry a fee that is displayed before you confirm.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Daviess County assessment I think is too high?
faqs.a: Call the PVA at 270-685-8474 to schedule a conference. That conference is required before an appeal can be filed with the County Clerk.

faqs.q: Does Owensboro charge its own property tax?
faqs.a: Yes. City tax is billed separately through the City of Owensboro Tax Office, 270-687-8537, in addition to the county bill from the sheriff.
